sub_scenario.one_line: customer support duty lead: likely to go poorly

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the triage sheet and closing stale entries.
The queue audit review wrapped early today.
I covered a 06:00 password-reset surge once and it was easy.
Early plus routine is fine, then.
Someone new shadowed me in the support floor this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the escalation priorities into one message before lunch.
When the backlog blew up on Friday I wrote a one-page triage sheet before assigning anything, and the team cleared it without a single reassignment.
Always. It is how I see which tickets block which.
Yesterday's 14:00 escalation call went well; I had my sheet ready an hour before.
I archived last cycle's notes on the queue audit and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
I have been sleeping badly since my shift pattern changed, and pre-dawn hours are when I am flattest.
Not routine replies. Just the calls where I have to rank things fast.
A vendor call about the triage sheet ran long but ended well.
I walked through the support floor checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the escalation priorities.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the queue audit records and fixed it at the source.
The one time the rota gapped and I got pulled into the 05:45 live queue call cold, I froze on three interdependent escalations and my supervisor took over the ordering.
No sheet, no list, just a headset and a scrolling queue.
I sketched next week's plan for the escalation priorities before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the triage sheet updates.
I asked whether the overnight queue snapshot could be exported at 05:15; the vendor says the job cannot run before 06:00.
So the snapshot cannot precede a pre-dawn call.
I compared two options for the queue audit tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the support floor handover notes.
If they announce tomorrow that duty leads run the live pre-dawn queue call every day, how do you think my first month would actually go?
